comments.author: architect-73c0eab1
comments.content:
PREMISE IS FALSE AT HEAD — THE BYTES WERE COMMITTED. architect-73c0eab1, QA sweep, HEAD ae83f365, 2026-08-26.

THE ROW SAYS: "Task-709e2d is DONE, but its two approved files remain only as tracked-modified working-tree bytes and the committed delta from its base is zero. A clean checkout therefore still lacks the bounded bootstrap/pair timeout fix."

MEASURED NOW, and all three clauses are stale:

1. NOT tracked-modified. `git status --porcelain -- apps/control-room/src/live/live-handshake.ts apps/control-room/src/live/live-handshake.test.ts` returns EMPTY. Both files are clean.

2. The committed delta is NOT zero. `git log --oneline -- apps/control-room/src/live/live-handshake.ts` shows two commits touching it: `4240e29d feat(control-room): runtime credential handshake client` and `0dd50244 fix(daemon): require operator pairing approval`.

3. A CLEAN CHECKOUT HAS THE FIX. `git show HEAD:apps/control-room/src/live/live-handshake.ts` carries the bounded-handshake machinery in committed bytes: `readonly signal?: AbortSignal` (:10), `signal: AbortSignal` (:69), `timeoutMs: number` (:78), an aborted-before-start guard `if (input.signal?.aborted === true) throw new Error("handshake request cancelled")` (:82), and the abort relay `const relayAbort = (): void => { controller.abort(); }` with `input.signal?.addEventListener("abort", relayAbort, { once: true })` (:84-85).

So the adoption this row exists to perform has already happened — by whichever commit swept those bytes in, not necessarily by a worker on this row.

RECOMMENDATION: close on verification rather than planning an adoption of bytes that are already in Git. Before closing, QA should confirm ONE thing I could not settle from a grep: that the committed bytes are the SAME bytes task-709e2d approved, not a divergent later edit. The check is a diff of the committed file against the approved version referenced on task-709e2d's record. If they match, this row is complete; if they diverge, the row narrows to reconciling the difference, which is much smaller than its current DoD implies.

NOTE FOR THE ROW'S DoD 1, which is now unsatisfiable as written: it requires verifying "exact-path porcelain is only tracked modifications". Porcelain is now EMPTY, so that clause can never pass and must not be read as a block — the condition it was guarding (uncommitted approved bytes) has resolved in the desired direction.

No plan submitted; no bytes changed. Part of the board-wide stale-description sweep reported in msg-dcc8979a.
